newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ICI sees higher Q2 prices.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ICI sees higher Q2 prices.

text.p: Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc said on Thursday prices for a number of key bulk chemicals were picking up in the second quarter and would continue to firm as the quarter progresses.
"We are confident that prices will be firmer in the second quarter and will affect our results," finance director Alan Spall said.
"(But) clearly it will take some time for the impact of the changes to come through," he added after ICI earlier said it expected profits to improve in the second half of the year.
Spall, however, declined to forecast second quarter results after pre-tax profit before exceptional items fell to 65 million stg in the first quarter from 202 million stg a year earlier.
"They are about in line with the market average" said Spall of the first-quarter results.

A strong pound, higher oil prices and depressed prices and margins in bulk chemicals hit profits. But Spall said he was optimistic about near-future prospects as solid growth was coming through from continental Europe.
"That gives us encouragement that it will provide an environment in which prices may well tighten," he said.
A number of contract prices have already moved up in April compared with March. Lower oil prices would also have a positive impact, Spall said.
"All the evidence is that input prices will be better for us," he said.
Spall declined to comment on recent press reports saying ICI had tabled a bid for Unilever's Unichema natural oils business.
Unichema is one of four chemicals businesses put up for sale by Unilever in February.
The operations offer high margins and are less volatile than the "heavy" industrial chemicals.
An acquisition of part of Unilever's chemicals operations would fit in well with ICI's stated strategy of moving more into "light" chemicals, analysts said earlier.
But Spall remained tightlipped. "I am not getting into discussion on a specific acquisition in specific businesses."
Spall repeated ICI's general strategy of focusing on "...value-creating acquisitions and organic growth in our strong leadership intermediate and surface coating business."
As part of its increased emphasis on "lighter" chemicals, ICI in February announced it would float its tioxide business within the next 18 months.
Spall said the float was on schedule. "All of the work is well in hand."
Together with polyester, tioxide -- a whitening agent for paints, plastics and ink -- is one of the bulk chemicals that have fallen victim to a sharp cyclical downtrend.
To fight difficult market conditions, ICI has made "excellent" progress in boosting productivity with staff numbers down five percent on an annual rate, Spall said.
"We are doing the right thing in terms of running the businesses we've got," he said.
-- Hans de Jongh, London newsroom +441 71 542 7717
